title: Regulatory Compliance Decision Tree
description: Decision tree for navigating regulatory requirements during life sciences CRM migration

nodes.question: Which regulatory domains apply to this migration?
nodes.guidance: Select all that apply. Most life sciences organizations fall under multiple regulatory domains.

nodes.question: Does the organization distribute product samples to healthcare professionals?
nodes.guidance: PDMA (Prescription Drug Marketing Act) requires complete audit trail for all sample transactions from manufacturer to HCP.

options.label: Yes — but phasing out physical samples

requirements: Complete sample transaction history must be migrated — no selective migration allowed
Every transaction must be traceable from receipt through disbursement to acknowledgment
HCP signature on sample receipt must be preserved as a digital record
Sample lot expiration dates must be validated and enforced
Representative inventory reconciliation must balance after migration
Sample limit enforcement must be configured and tested before go-live
Annual inventory reconciliation reporting must work in new platform
Historical sample transactions must still be migrated for audit purposes
Active lot management may be simplified but lot tracking is still required
Transition to digital-only must be documented and sample program closure date recorded
Remaining sample inventory must be accounted for and reconciled
No sample management migration required
Verify no sample-related data exists in legacy system before skipping

nodes.question: Does the organization operate in the US and provide anything of value to HCPs?
nodes.guidance: The Physician Payments Sunshine Act (Open Payments) requires reporting of all transfers of value to covered recipients.

options.label: Yes — but only through third-party aggregator

requirements: All HCP spend data for the current and prior reporting period must be migrated completely
Event attendee data with meal/travel costs must be preserved
Speaker program payments must be traceable
Consulting and advisory board fees must be linked to the correct HCP
Research payments must be categorized correctly (direct vs. indirect)
The reporting period cannot have gaps — migration cutover must be planned around Sunshine Act deadlines
Aggregate spend reporting must produce identical results in new platform
Verify third-party aggregator data feed will work with new platform
Ensure data export format is compatible or transformation is in place
Historical data may still need migration for internal analytics
Check for country-specific transparency requirements (e.g., EFPIA in EU, JPMA in Japan)
Many countries have their own HCP payment disclosure requirements
Data migration must support country-specific reporting formats

nodes.question: Which data privacy regulations apply?
nodes.guidance: Select the primary regulatory framework. Many organizations must comply with multiple frameworks.

requirements: Explicit opt-in consent required — no default opt-in during migration
If legacy consent records lack explicit evidence of opt-in, set to 'Not Captured' status
Right to erasure (Art. 17) must be implementable in new platform
Data portability (Art. 20) must be supported
Consent expiration tracking must be configured (renewal periods vary by use case)
Data processing agreements with new platform vendor must be in place
Cross-border data transfer mechanisms (SCCs, BCRs) must be established
Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) should be conducted before migration
Privacy by Design principles must be followed in platform configuration
Data retention policies must be configured per data category
Right to know — HCPs can request what data is stored about them
Right to delete — deletion requests must be fulfillable in new platform
Right to opt-out of sale — if data is shared with third parties, opt-out must be tracked
Vermont prescriber confidentiality laws may apply to certain data
Do Not Sell flag must be migrated if it exists in legacy system
Consent must be obtained for cross-border data transfers to countries without adequate protections
Purpose of use must be specified and migrated consent must align with stated purposes
Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC) guidelines must be followed
Anonymization requirements differ from GDPR — verify approach
Legal basis for processing must be documented (consent, legitimate interest, etc.)
Data subjects must be able to access, correct, and delete their data
Data Protection Officer (DPO) must be appointed
International data transfers require adequate safeguards
Apply the most restrictive requirement across all applicable jurisdictions
GDPR is typically the most restrictive baseline — start there
Country-specific consent defaults must be configured per market
Data residency requirements may require regional deployment
Build a privacy requirements matrix mapping each regulation to platform capabilities
Engage legal counsel in each jurisdiction before finalizing consent migration approach

nodes.question: Does the organization need electronic signature compliance?
nodes.guidance: 21 CFR Part 11 governs electronic records and electronic signatures in FDA-regulated industries.

options.label: Partial — audit trail required but not full e-signature

requirements: Complete audit trail for all record changes (who, what, when, why)
Electronic signatures must be linked to unique individual credentials
Signature records must be tamper-evident and time-stamped
System access controls must enforce individual accountability
Backup and recovery procedures must ensure record integrity
Training documentation for system users must be maintained
Validation documentation (IQ/OQ/PQ) for the new platform must be completed
Standard Operating Procedures must be updated for the new platform
Audit trail must capture record creation, modification, and deletion with timestamps
User authentication must be enforced
Field-level audit history must be enabled for regulated objects
Data backup and recovery procedures must be documented and tested

nodes.question: Does the organization sell or distribute medical devices?
nodes.guidance: Medical device companies have additional regulatory requirements around Unique Device Identification (UDI), post-market surveillance, and adverse event reporting.

requirements: UDI (Unique Device Identification) data must be migrated and maintained
Complaint and adverse event data must be traceable
Post-market surveillance data collection must continue through migration
Device-specific regulatory requirements vary by classification (I, II, III)
Notified Body audit trails must be preserved
Care program and assessment data for medical devices requires special handling
Both pharmaceutical and medical device regulations apply
Combination product tracking requires both drug lot and device UDI data
FDA Center jurisdiction (CDER vs CDRH) determines primary regulatory framework
Supply chain tracking must cover both components

nodes.question: Which country-specific pharma regulations apply?
nodes.guidance: Beyond global frameworks, many countries have specific pharmaceutical industry regulations.

requirements: JPMA Fair Competition Code compliance for HCP interactions
Japanese Personal Information Protection Act (APPI) consent requirements
MR (Medical Representative) activity reporting requirements
Japanese language support and double-byte character handling in all migrated data
Transparence-Santé reporting of all HCP/HCO payments and benefits
Anti-Gifts Law caps on meal values and gift values
CNIL (French data protection authority) requirements for data processing
French language support for all user-facing content
FSA-Kodex (Voluntary Self-Regulation for the Pharmaceutical Industry) compliance
Transparency reporting of HCP payments
Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) requirements in addition to GDPR
German language support for all user-facing content
ABPI Code of Practice for pharmaceutical marketing
MHRA reporting requirements
UK GDPR (post-Brexit) consent requirements
NHS engagement and contracting requirements if applicable
Build a country-by-country regulatory matrix
Configure consent defaults per country in the target platform
Transparency reporting requirements vary — map each country's requirements
Language and locale support must cover all operating countries
Data residency requirements may restrict where data can be stored
Consider a phased regional rollout rather than a simultaneous global go-live
